title: Chihuahua State Investigation Agency Director & Two US Embassy “Officials” Die in Accident
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
_This article originally appeared in the April 20, 2026 edition of Sin
Embargo._

Pedro Ramón Oseguera Cervantes, director of the Chihuahua State Investigation
Agency (AEI), died along with three other people, including two members of the
staff of the U.S. Embassy in Mexico, as a result of a car accident in the
municipality of Morelos. The incident was mourned by Ronald Johnson, U.S.
Ambassador to Mexico.

According to reports, Cervantes and the other deceased individuals were
returning from an operation in which two drug labs were discovered and
destroyed. The car they were traveling in reportedly lost control and plunged
into a ravine.

Travelling with the director of the Chihuahua State Investigation Agency (AEI)
were Genaro Méndez Montes, an AEI agent, and two instructor officers from the
United States Embassy in Mexico, whose names have not been revealed.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ronald-johnson-
death-squad.jpg)_Ronald Johnson, US Ambassador to Mexico, former Green Beret &
CIA Agent with asset Nayib Bukele_

**Ambassador Johnson Regrets the Accident**

Through social media, Ronald Johnson, the United States Ambassador to Mexico,
lamented the incident that cost the lives of two members of the Embassy, ​​and
acknowledged the work of all the people who died in the accident.

"We deeply regret the tragic loss of two U.S. Embassy staff members, the
Director of the Chihuahua State Investigation Agency (AEI), and one of the
agency's agents in this accident. We recognize their dedication and tireless
efforts in addressing one of the greatest challenges of our time," Johnson
said.

In his statement, the Ambassador also noted that this accident is a "reminder"
of the dangers constantly faced by Mexican and American officials who dedicate
their lives to fighting drug trafficking and protecting the population.

He also noted that the tragedy helps authorities strengthen their
"determination to continue their mission and advance our shared commitment to
security and justice, to protect our people."

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-76.png)

**Chihuahua Prosecutor Also Commented on the Matter**

For his part, César Jáuregui Moreno, Attorney General of the state of
Chihuahua, also said he regretted the death of the two members of the State
Investigation Agency and the two members of the US Embassy in Mexico.

"From here, our deepest condolences and prayers for the families of those who
died in this tragic accident," the Prosecutor commented during a press
conference held this morning.

Jáuregui highlighted the career and service of the fallen officers, especially
the director of the AEI, whose "life, dedication and commitment to the safety
of the people of Chihuahua" he emphasized.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/04/image-75.png)_Publication from the Chihuahua State
Attorney General 's Office regarding the death of the director of the State
Investigation Agency (AEI). Photo: Chihuahua State Attorney General's Office_
